description: SIDERA VI is driven by curiosity, innovation, and the spirit of discovery. For the Martian Map challenge, we envision an interactive exploration companion that transforms NASA data into practical tools for navigating Mars. From real terrain maps and simulated positioning to solar time, orientation, and mission planning, our goal is to help future explorers understand their surroundings and make informed decisions. We believe the next great leap begins with the courage to explore the unknown.
summary:
What would it take for our children to explore Mars and find their way back to base?

The Urquia and Flores families created SIDERA VI: Martian Explorer to turn that question into a hands on learning experience. For the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, we built an educational app that combines NASA Mars Trek imagery and MOLA elevation data and calculations based on NASA Mars24 algorithms complemented by historical atmosphere data from MACDA with scientific missions and simulated surface navegation. 

Explorers choose from five Martian regions and complete scientific objectives. Their physical steps and devices orientation translate into estimated movement across a Martian map. Along the way, they can check coordinates, elevation information, local solar time, daylight estimates and regional temperature estimates, while following direct guidance toward a destination or back to base. 

Our mission test pilots, Dan and Adrian, participated in hands on testing. Their involvement keeps the project aligned to reality and connected to the people we built it for, curious learners. 

SIDERA VI brings planetary science into a shared family adventure. Its maps and environmental information have scientific foundations, astronaut movement remains an educational simulation, not actual positioning on Mars.
details:
SIDERA VI: Martian Explorer is an educational smartphone and tablet app that runs walking on Earth into simulated exploration on Mars. Participants choose among 5 real Martian regions, explore mission areas spanning 500 meters to 1 km in radius and complete 15 scientific objectives across the missions.

Using pedestrian dear reckoning, the app combines step count, adjustable stride length and device orientation to estimate movement across a Martian map without terrestrial GPS. Explorers view simulated coordinates, heading, distance and direct guidance toward destinations or back to Habitat Base.

NASA Mars Trek imagery provides the maps, MOLA supplies elevation information and calculations based on NASA Mars24 algorithms that provide local solar time and daylight estimates. Historical MACDA atmospheric reanalysis supports regional temperature estimates. Shared crew sessions allow participants to see virtual teammates and send location signals.

SIDERA VI connects scientific information with actions children can understand, walking, choosing a destination, checking daylight and finding their way back. Missions encourage curiosity, spatial awareness, collaboration and discussion about how environmental conditions influence exploration.

Families can learn together while discovering how planetary data becomes useful information.

The Urquia and Flores families created SIDERA VI so our children could participate in space science through hands on experimentation. Our Mission Test Pilots, Dan and Adrian, participated in testing and helped keep the experience focused on young learners. We hope to inspire students and families to explore open scientific resources, ask questions and create their own project.

We developed the app using Flutter and Dart. Apple Core Motion and CMPedometer support iPhone movement input, while Firebase Realtime Database supports shared crew sessions.

Scientific resources include NASA Mars Trek CTX/HiRISE imagery, MOLA elevation grids, NASA Mars24 algorithm documentation and MACDA v2.0 atmospheric reanalysis.

Hardware included iPhone, iPads and Android smartphone for testing. Codex assisted with coding and debugging under team supervision, ChatGPT supported visual asset creation and translation.

We considered usability for children, scientific transparency, device limitations, connectivity and responsible interpretation of results. Movement has been demostrated on iPhone, Android behavior and walking based crew synchronization require future validation.

Navigation provides direct guidance without checking obstacles. Solar estimates exclude terrain shadows, temperatures represent historical conditions rather than live weather and crew sharing requires connectivity. The educational SOS doesn't contact emergency services.

SIDERA VI combines physical movement, planetary science and collaborative missions. Children become participants in an exploration story, using their own steps to navigate a Martian landscape and scientific information to understand their surroundings.
projectRefs: MACDA v2.0 (Mars Analysis Correction Data Assimilation)
